ecdhPublicKey.description:
When establishing a headless session, the client must first provide
their ECDH public key. The server will then generate an ephemeral
ECHD keypair and use the client's public key to establish a symmetric
key.

This symmetric key will be used to encrypt the idtoken and stored the
encrypted idtoken in the database for a short period, as well as
returning it to the client.

After the idtoken is encrypted, the server will discard both the shared
symmetric key and the ephemeral ECDH private key. The server ECDH will
be sent back to the client.

The client, with their private key, can use this public key to
establish the same symmetric key, which can be used to decrypt
the idtoken.

echd_public_key is the client's ECDH public key.

registries.description: Empty for an unenrolled organization; otherwise its single Registry.

chainguard.platform.oci.v2alpha1.ListRep.description: ListReposResponse contains a page of private repository metadata.

totalCount.description: Total matching repositories, not just the current page length.

chainguard.platform.oci.v2alpha1.Registr.description: EnrollRegistryRequest selects an existing root organization for enrollment.
SetRegistryStateRequest changes an enrolled Registry's lifecycle state.

state.description: ACTIVE or DISABLED; STATE_UNSPECIFIED is not an update.

chainguard.platform.oci.v2alpha1.Registr.description: Registry is an operator-enrolled private registry owned by an organization.

domain.description: Service-assigned hostname, without a scheme or path.

uid.description: Stable Registry UIDP assigned by the service.

updateTime.description: Time the Registry metadata last changed.

chainguard.platform.oci.v2alpha1.Registr.description:
State controls Registry content serving and writes.

 - STATE_UNSPECIFIED: State was not specified.
 - ACTIVE: Registry permits authorized content serving and writes.
 - DISABLED: Content serving and writes are refused; metadata and cleanup remain
available.

chainguard.platform.oci.v2alpha1.Repo.description: Repo is private repository metadata, separate from the Chainguard catalog.

name.description: Repository path relative to the Registry, for example "team/api".

uid.description: Stable repository UIDP assigned by the service.

updateTime.description: Time the repository metadata last changed.

chainguard.platform.oidc.TokenPair.description:
ExchangeRefreshToken returns a pair of token, in order to allow
refresh token to also be rotated.

parameters.description:
One or more group scopes to restrict the returned token to.
If scope and scopes are both provided, the union of their values is
considered, after deduplication.

The returned token will include role bindings for the requested scopes,
if any exist, that are either granted directly at that scope or inherited from
its ancestors. That is, a role binding granted at a "lower" scope in the ancestry
applies to all descendants of that scope.

For example, given a role binding on group `foo` with id `foo/rb-id-1`
and a role binding on group `foo/bar` with id `foo/bar/rb-id-2`:
 - given scopes = [foo, foo/bar] => {foo: [foo/rb-id-1], foo/bar: [foo/bar/rb-id-2]}
 - given scopes = [foo/bar] => {foo/bar: [foo/rb-id-1, foo/bar/rb-id-2]}
parameters.name: scopes

parameters.description:
delegated requests the delegated exchange mode when assuming `identity`.
The assumed identity's own role bindings are not consulted; instead the
returned token's capabilities are a per-scope subset of the presented
credential's capabilities, selected by `scopes` and `cap` (both
required), and its expiry never exceeds the presented credential's. A
request for any capability or scope the presented credential does not
hold is rejected, never trimmed. The presented credential must be a
delegation grant: a token minted by this issuer whose only audience is
"<issuer>/delegation/<name>", pinned by the identity's claim_match, and
the identity must be marked delegation_only. A token minted by a
delegated exchange is never accepted as a grant. No refresh token is
issued. The returned token's subject is the assumed identity, its `act`
claim is the presented credential's verified claims, and its
`act_chain` records the transfer.
parameters.name: delegated

parameters.description:
task is an optional opaque identifier for the work the delegated token
is minted for (e.g. a session id), recorded as the token's `task` claim
for attribution. It is never used for authorization. At most 128 bytes
of letters, digits, and `. _ : / @ -`. Only honored with `delegated`.
parameters.name: task

parameters.description:
refresh_token_rotation declares that the client handles refresh-token
rotation: it stores one refresh token per family under a lock shared by
its processes, persists the successor every refresh returns, and
discards a token the issuer refuses as REFRESH_TOKEN_SUPERSEDED. The
issuer rotates a refresh-token family only if the exchange that created
it set this; a family created without it is echoed back unchanged on
every refresh. A client must not set it unless it does all three, since
a rotated family whose superseded token is presented again is revoked.
A successor's expiry may be later than its parent's: a rotated family's
session slides while it is used, up to its organizations' session
length.
parameters.name: refreshTokenRotation
